name: screws:M2 screws form enough thread in the print

name: screws:printed washer keeps the pawl on its pivot
detail: the flange of the printed pivot washer (Ø7.0) overlaps the pawl's bore (Ø5.3) by 0.65 mm all round, however the washer sits on its screw; a standard M2 washer (Ø5.0, ISO 7089) would be 0.15 mm smaller than the bore. The pawl keeps 0.30 mm of play above the washer, and the servo arm passes 0.90 mm from it at rest and at release

name: screws:a hex key reaches the speaker clamp screws
detail: with the core on the bench (steps 4 to 6) the long arm of a 1.5 mm hex key (45 mm) lies free behind each of the two screws: blocked by nothing; its short arm can swing through 150° (60° are enough to take a new grip). A screwdriver in line with the screw meets charger, chassis; held 20° upwards, as a ball-end hex driver allows, it meets nothing. A cross-head screw cannot be driven here: these two screws need a hex socket

name: screws:heat-set inserts fit their bosses
detail: eight M3 inserts of Ø5.0 in holes of Ø4.4: 0.30 mm of plastic to melt per side, 2.0 mm of wall round the hole (at least 1.3 mm, research/06 section 4.1). At the rim: 6 mm inserts, 1.0 mm free under them, 6.0 mm of thread for the stack screws. Low on the front wall: 5 mm inserts, 1.2 mm free under them, 3.8 mm of thread for the screws of the tongue

name: pins:towers enclose the hinge pins
detail: round the Ø2.15 bore of each tower the stage is solid over at least 1.6 mm, at every angle and over the whole thickness of the tower (2.2 mm). Half of each knuckle stands out of the dome of the stage; it keeps 0.51 mm from the wall of the lid with the lid closed, 30° and 65° open and at the stop

name: pins:two hinge pins carry lid and spring
detail: each Ø2 x 8 pin slides in 2.2 mm of its hinge tower (bore Ø2.15), carries one rib of the lid over its full 3.4 mm (bore Ø2.3) and stands on the floor of a blind hole 1.80 mm deep in the spring sleeve, of which 1.35 mm are a press fit (Ø1.95) and the rest a funnel; its outer end then stands 0.25 mm out of the tower, so that pliers can press home a pin that is a little shorter as well

name: pins:the sleeve keeps the hinge pins
detail: the sleeve (Ø4.0 x 6.3) lies between the ribs of the lid with 0.15 mm of play at each end and does not pass their Ø2.3 bores: pushed 0.55 mm along the axis it meets a rib (2.9 mm3). A pin cannot go further in, because 2.7 mm of sleeve lie between the two blind holes. To free the lid it would have to move 5.35 mm outwards, so it has to be pulled out of its hole in the sleeve first. That press fit is the only thing that holds it: no check here can show how firmly

name: pins:why the hinge has two pins
detail: the hinge axis lies inside the lid and meets its wall 16.8 mm from the middle; beside a hinge tower a Ø2 pin has 4.9 mm of room before it touches the wall. A pin that goes through both ribs cannot be put in, at any length. A waiting pin stands 5.8 mm out of its tower

name: pins:waiting pins clear the lid
detail: with the pins waiting in the towers (flush with the inner faces of the towers) the lid keeps 0.25 mm from them; the relief inside the lid wall that makes this room leaves 1.3 mm of wall (measured: 100.0 % of that shell is solid), so nothing shows outside. The wall behind the knuckles is 1.0 mm as before

name: pins:lid slides onto the hinge from behind
detail: lid held 65° open and brought forwards from 16 mm behind its seat, level and up to 20° from below: 0 collisions with the stage or the waiting pins

name: pins:tools reach the hinge pins
detail: without force: a screwdriver blade of 2.5 x 0.8 mm reaches the end of each waiting pin with the lid 65° open and follows it until the pin has passed its rib, 3.6 mm further in, coming from 75, 90, 105° (directions round the hinge, 90° is straight from above, tried in steps of 15°). With force: from there the pins slide 0.6 mm more and are then pressed 1.35 mm into the sleeve; plier jaws of 4.0 x 3.0 mm reach both pin ends over that last part, lid 90° open from 90, 105, 120, 135°; lid 95° open from 90, 105, 120, 135°. The jaws start 21.4 mm apart. They stop when both pins stand on the floors of their holes

The switch needs 4.8 mT at most. Not covered: two magnets with unlike poles down, which cancel on the axis; the reader's IRQ line is wired as the second way to wake
